Qual è la proteina migliore per il cane? La risposta probabilmente non è quella che ti aspetti. 🐶🥚 5° posto: legumi e proteine vegetali Possono contribuire alla quota proteica della dieta, ma generalmente hanno valore biologico e digeribilità inferiori rispetto alle fonti animali. Inoltre fibra e alcuni composti vegetali possono influenzare la disponibilità di alcuni nutrienti. 4° posto: latticini Possono essere fonti proteiche interessanti quando ben tollerati e scelti correttamente, ma non sono adatti a tutti i cani e raramente rappresentano l’unica fonte proteica della giornata. 3° posto: pesce Ottima fonte di proteine. A seconda della specie scelta può apportare anche grassi e micronutrienti molto interessanti, ma va sempre inserito nelle quantità corrette. 2° posto: carne e frattaglie Forniscono proteine di elevata qualità e numerosi micronutrienti. Ma riempire la ciotola di carne e organi non basta per ottenere una dieta completa. 1° posto: uovo È una delle fonti proteiche di riferimento grazie al profilo completo di aminoacidi essenziali e all’elevata digeribilità. La vera risposta, però, è che non esiste una fonte proteica migliore in assoluto. Esiste quella più utile all’interno di una dieta varia, completa e formulata sul singolo cane. Dopo aver visto le 10 idee di colazioni proteiche, in questa seconda parte parliamo di come capire quante proteine assumere durante la giornata. ㅤ ㅤ Le proteine sono indispensabili per il mantenimento e la crescita della massa muscolare, ma anche per la regolazione ormonale, la risposta immunitaria e la sazietà. ㅤ Tuttavia, la quantità ottimale non è uguale per tutte: dipende da peso, livello di attività fisica e obiettivo (dimagrimento, mantenimento o aumento della massa muscolare). 🌸 ㅤ 👉 Le linee guida più aggiornate indicano per una donna che si allena regolarmente un apporto compreso tra 1,6 e 2 g di proteine per kg di peso corporeo al giorno. ㅤ 📍 Esempi pratici: – Donna di 60 kg che si allena 3–4 volte a settimana → circa 90–100 g di proteine al giorno – Donna che si allena con maggiore intensità o segue una fase di ricomposizione corporea → fino a 120 g, sempre valutando la dieta complessiva ㅤ 💡 L’aspetto più importante non è solo la quantità totale, ma come le proteine vengono distribuite nei vari pasti: ogni pasto principale dovrebbe includere una fonte proteica, accompagnata da carboidrati complessi e grassi buoni per un equilibrio ottimale. ㅤ Nel carosello di oggi troverai alcune colazioni proteiche con il pane, un alimento che molte donne amano ma spesso evitano pensando che “faccia ingrassare”. ㅤ In realtà, il pane può far parte di una dieta equilibrata e completa: basta abbinarlo a una buona fonte di proteine e grassi per ottenere un pasto saziante, bilanciato e perfetto per chi si allena 🥖✨ ㅤ Nei prossimi caroselli parleremo di come distribuire le proteine nei pasti della giornata, per capire come organizzare colazioni, pranzi e cene in modo semplice e realistico. ㅤ ㅤ Per informazioni sui nostri percorsi nutrizionali o di allenamento, compila il form che torvi nel link in bio! Why do we cling to meat even when we want to go greener? 🥩 Most of us know that plant-based food is healthier and better for the planet, yet many still reach for the steak. A new study from the University of Copenhagen reveals that the barrier isn't just the taste of meat—it is a lack of "meal knowledge." Researchers found that while people recognize ingredients like tofu or chickpeas, they often don't know how to combine them into a satisfying, complete meal. It is like having the screws and planks for a chair but no manual on how to build it. Key findings from the research: - The Meal Gap: Knowing an ingredient is not enough. Familiarity with full plant-based recipes is the biggest predictor of making the switch. - Food Neophobia: In some cultures, a natural fear of "unfamiliar" foods keeps meat at the center of the plate. - Cultural Differences: While both Denmark and Australia are high meat-consumers, the psychological barriers differ based on how much international cuisine people already eat. The study suggests that to change our habits, we don't just need more vegetables—we need to rethink what a "meal" looks like from the ground up. Zahlreiche pflanzliche Lebensmittel enthalten sie, darunter auch Hülsenfrüchte. Die sogenannten Anti-Nährstoffe werden aber durch Einweichen und Erhitzen reduziert bzw. zerstört. Zahlreiche Studien liefern Hinweise darauf, dass der Verzehr lektinhaltiger pflanzlicher Lebensmittel – darunter Hülsenfrüchte, Vollkornprodukte und Nüsse – einen gesundheitlichen Nutzen bringen, z.B. ein geringeres Risiko für Herz-Kreislauf-Erkrankungen oder Typ-2-Diabetes. No Bake Chocolate Tart is for the chocolate lovers.  It’s decadent and delicious, as well as smooth and creamy.  Some key ingredients included avocado, almond milk, unsweetened cocoa powder and sugar free maple syrup.  The crust is a blend of almonds, coconut flake and cocoa powder and it is incredibly tasty. No Bake Chocolate Tart Ingredients: 1 1/3 Cups of raw almonds, unsalted 1/2 Cup of unsweetened coconut flakes 2 Tablespoons of unsweetened cocoa powder 1/3 Cup + 1 tablespoon of sugar free maple syrup or you can use agave syrup 2 Tablespoon of coconut oil, melted Chocolate Avocado Mousse 1 Cup of avocado, about 3 to 4 avocados (240g 8.5 oz) 1/3 Cup of unsweetened almond milk or you can use rice milk 1/3 Cup + 1 Tablespoon of unsweetened cocoa powder 1/3 Cup + 2 tablespoons of sugar free maple syrup or agave 3 Tablespoon of coconut oil, melted Topping: 1/2 Cup 85% dark chocolate bar, shaved or cut into chunks Directions: -In a blender or a food processor, add all the dry ingredients, raw almonds, unsweetened coconut and cocoa powder. Blend for 30 seconds until the almonds are a thick meal. Then add the maple syrup and melted coconut oil. Then blend again until it’s a sticky dough. If it’s too loose, or dry adjust by adding 1 tablespoon of water if necessary then blend again. Add the sticky dough to the pan, 20 cm (8 inches). I used a 9 inch pan and added the crust to the bottom of the pan. If it’s too sticky, you can also place a piece of parchment paper between your fingers and the dough to prevent sticking to your fingers if desired. Press the dough until it covers the entire pan then put in the refrigerator to set. -To make the chocolate mousse, scoop out the ripe avocado flesh and add to the blender along with the sugar free maple syrup, cocoa powder, unsweetened almond milk and melted coconut oil. Blend ingredients well until coconut is combined. Then pour the chocolate mouse into the prepared pie crust. I Found a Drawer in My Mother's Kitchen Last Easter. There Were Six Years of Bloodwork Results in It. None of Them Had Been Opened. I'm 47. My mother is 74. She lives an hour east of me in the house I grew up in. I drove out for Easter last year. Me, my husband Brian, our son Ethan who's sixteen, our daughter Hannah who's thirteen. We brought the ham. We brought Hannah's deviled eggs — she'd made them by herself for the first time and was nervous about whether the paprika was even. We brought a bottle of Riesling because my mother has been a half-glass-with-dinner woman for forty years and won't buy her own. I want to tell you what happened with the drawer. But I want to back up first. Because if I just tell you about the drawer it'll sound like a thing that happened in a single afternoon. What was actually happening was a thing that had been building since 2019. My father died in May of that year. Five years before that Easter. He'd been sick for about eighteen months. Pancreatic. There's not much you can say about pancreatic that isn't in every cancer memoir already, and I'm not going to add to the genre. What I'll say is that my mother, who had been a second-grade teacher for thirty-eight years and the most relentlessly competent person I knew, took care of him at home all the way through. And then walked into the kitchen the morning after his funeral and started reorganizing the spice rack. That was her grief. She reorganized the spice rack. She alphabetized her bookshelves. She sorted forty years of photographs into archival boxes by year. Then she sat down in my father's reading chair for the first time and didn't get up for about two weeks. By two weeks I don't mean literally. I mean the spirit of it. She got up to eat. She got up to call me. She got up to walk to the mailbox. But she sat in that chair for what amounted to two weeks. And when she got up again she was a smaller woman than she'd been the day my father died. She didn't get bigger again. That's the part nobody told me about losing a parent — that the surviving parent can shrink, and that it might be permanent. About a year after my father died, my mother had her annual checkup with Dr. Patel. She'd been seeing him for about a decade by then. She likes him. He's the kind of doctor who remembers you used to teach second grade and asks about your former students. Her cholesterol numbers had crept up. She told me about it on the phone. She said it like it was nothing. "Patel says it's a little high. He says we should keep an eye on it." I said: "Are you going to need medication?" She said: "He mentioned it. He said let's try the basics first. I told him that sounded right to me." I said: "Okay." That was 2020. In 2021 the numbers had crept up again. She told me again. Same conversation. Same "let's try the basics first." In 2022 she stopped telling me what the numbers were. I asked her once that fall what Dr. Patel had said at her last appointment. She said: "He's a good doctor. We have an arrangement." I didn't ask her what the arrangement was. I thought I knew. I thought she was managing it. What I didn't know — what I didn't let myself know — is that "managing it" had quietly become "not opening the envelopes." So. Easter. We had dinner at four. Ham, the deviled eggs, asparagus, her mother's roll recipe that she's made every Easter since 1972. Hannah was watching her grandmother eat in that way teenagers watch the adults around them when they're trying to figure something out and aren't going to ask. Hannah leaned over to me at one point and whispered: "Is Grammy okay?" I said: "What do you mean?" Hannah said: "She's barely eating." I looked. She was right. My mother had pushed her ham around her plate and eaten about two bites. She'd taken one deviled egg, eaten half of it, set the rest down. She'd taken half a roll. She'd had her half-glass of Riesling and then put her hand over the rim when Brian went to refill it. I'd been so busy keeping up the table conversation — Brian's mother had broken her hip in March and was at a rehab facility, Ethan had gotten his driver's license, Hannah was about to start a summer art camp — that I hadn't looked at my mother for the first forty minutes of dinner. When I looked, she was watching us. She wasn't eating. She wasn't drinking. She was just watching. The way you watch something you're memorizing. I want to be honest that I didn't know what to do with that, in the moment. So I did what I usually do, which is keep talking. After dinner she went to bed at 8:15. Hannah looked at me with the look of a thirteen-year-old who has noticed something and would like the adults to also notice it. I told her I'd noticed. I told her Grammy was just tired from cooking all day. I told her we'd come back soon. I didn't believe what I was telling her. Hannah didn't either. We both pretended. I offered to clean up. I was loading the dishwasher when I realized I needed to put the gravy boat away. The gravy boat is the one with the chip on the lip that my grandmother gave my mother in 1969. It lives in the dining room hutch. I went to put it back and it wasn't there. I came back to the kitchen and started checking drawers. I opened the third drawer down on the right side. The one she calls the junk drawer. The one with the rubber bands and the takeout menus from restaurants that closed in 2014. The gravy boat wasn't in it. What was in it was a stack of envelopes. White. Standard letter-sized. Office-of-Dr-Patel return address on every one. Some of them had a window envelope with a printout showing through. Most of them were sealed. I counted them later, in my head, on the drive home. There were eleven. Eleven envelopes spanning about six years. Nine of them had never been opened. I stood there in my mother's kitchen with the dishwasher running and a gravy boat in my hand that I'd put down on the counter without realizing. I closed the drawer. I went and checked the hutch one more time and the gravy boat was there. It had been there the whole time. I'd looked right past it. I put the gravy boat away. I went into the living room. My mother was already in bed. Brian and Ethan and Hannah were watching something on Hannah's phone. I sat on the couch next to Brian and put my head on his shoulder and didn't say anything for the rest of the evening. On the drive home I told him about the drawer. He said: "What do you want to do?" I said: "I don't know yet." I sat with the drawer for about three weeks. I didn't bring it up with my mother. I knew what would happen if I did. She'd say "those are private." She'd be right. She'd also be hiding from herself. I called her on a Tuesday and asked her how the last checkup had gone. She said: "Fine, honey. Patel said everything was fine." I said: "When was the last one?" She paused. She said: "I'd have to check the calendar." I said: "Okay, Mom." I hung up and I knew. She hadn't been in. She hadn't been in for a while. I'm going to be careful about what I claim happened next, because what happened next was that I, a 47-year-old accountant in Madison, Wisconsin, with no medical training, decided I was going to do something about my mother's cholesterol from an hour away. That's a sentence that should make any reasonable person nervous, and I want to say up front that the way it went well was that at every step I made my mother talk to her actual doctor and not to me. I started reading. I read about cholesterol in women over 70. I read about what people on the edge of being told to start medication do. I read about diet and exercise and the things you can stack on top of the basics. I read about beetroot. Not because it was trendy. Because it kept coming up. Beetroot has been studied for decades for things related to cardiovascular wellness. The compounds in beetroot — called betalains — appear to play a role in supporting the body's natural antioxidant balance. That's about as much as I'm going to claim to understand, because I'm an accountant, not a biochemist. I read for two evenings. I came across a small brand called Rosabella. What got my attention about them, embarrassingly, was a footnote about processing. They cold-press their beets at low temperatures. The reason that matters — and I had to read it twice to follow it — is that betalains are heat-sensitive. Faster processing methods can degrade them. Rosabella decided to do it the slow way. A small farming community in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania. Cold-pressed at low temperatures. Two capsules with water in the morning. Before I did anything else, I called my own doctor's office. I'm being honest about the order of operations. I didn't call my mother. I called my own doctor. I asked about it for me. I've had my own creeping numbers the last two years and figured I might as well start there. My doctor said yes, it was reasonable, food-based, fine to add. I ordered a bottle for myself. I took it for three weeks before I said a word to my mother. I wanted to know what it felt like before I asked her to try it. What it felt like was nothing dramatic. I noticed, around week two, that I wasn't bracing my back when I got out of bed in the morning. I noticed I was getting through 4 p.m. without the gummy bear emergency I'd been keeping in my desk drawer for a year. Small. Soft. Not magic. But enough to make me drive out to my mother's house on a Saturday in May. I brought groceries. I brought tulips. I brought my own bottle of the supplement. We had coffee at her kitchen table. I told her — and I had practiced this in the car, so I'm going to give you the practiced version because the practiced version is what I said — I told her that my numbers had been creeping a little. That my doctor had mentioned the basics. That I'd been reading about things and had come across a supplement. That I'd asked my own doctor about it and she'd said it was reasonable. That I'd been taking it for a few weeks. That I felt a little more like myself in the mornings. My mother listened. She didn't say much. Then I did the thing I'd practiced hardest. I said: "Mom. I want to be honest with you. I called Dr. Patel's office before I came over. I asked the nurse what she thought of this for somebody your age with your history. She said it was something Patel would probably be fine with — but I told her I wasn't asking on your behalf. I told her you would call him yourself if you wanted to know. I just wanted to know first." My mother set her coffee down. She looked at me for a long time. She said: "Karen. You called my doctor's office." I said: "I called your doctor's office about a supplement. I didn't ask anything about you. The nurse didn't tell me anything about you. She wouldn't have. I wouldn't have asked." She was quiet for a longer time. Then she said — and this is the sentence I keep coming back to — "I haven't been to see Patel in fourteen months." I didn't say anything. She said: "I know. You don't have to look at me like that." I said: "I'm not looking at you like anything." She said: "Yes you are." We sat there. Eventually she said: "I'll call Patel on Monday. Leave the bottle. If he says yes, I'll take it. If he says no, you can have it back." I left the bottle on the counter with the receipt taped to it. I drove home. On Monday at 4:15 p.m. she called me. She said: "I have an appointment with Patel on Thursday. He wants to see me before he says anything about the supplement. He said the supplement was probably fine but he hadn't seen me in over a year and he wanted bloodwork." I said: "Okay, Mom." She said: "Don't say anything." I said: "I'm not saying anything." She said: "I can hear you not saying anything." I laughed, the way you laugh when you're trying not to cry. Dr. Patel ran the bloodwork. The numbers were what they were. He wasn't alarmed but he was honest. He said the basics had been doing some of the work but he'd be paying closer attention from here on. He said the supplement was a sensible thing to add. He said: "Marjorie, I'm not going to ask why you haven't been in in fourteen months. I'm just glad you're here now. Let's see what we can do together." She told me about it on Thursday evening on the phone. She started the bottle on Friday morning. I want to tell you about a Saturday in August. I drove out to my mother's house unannounced. I'd been doing more drop-in visits because I liked seeing her in her natural state, with no time to prepare. I pulled into the driveway. Her Buick was there. I didn't go to the front door. I went around the back, through the gate by the garage. I found her in the rose bed. The rose bed is on the south side of the house, against the cinderblock foundation. It was planted by her father — my grandfather — in 1962, when my mother was twelve. She has tended it every summer since he died in 1989. Until 2022, when she let it start going. The quack grass had been crowding the roses for two years. The bed had been getting smaller every summer. I'd watched it happen and not said anything because I didn't know what to say. My mother was on her hands and knees in the dirt. Her gloves were off. There was dirt under her fingernails. Her hair, which she'd let go gray over the last three years, was pulled back in a kerchief I recognized as one of my father's old bandannas. She was pulling quack grass out of the bed by the roots, piling it next to her on the lawn. She was humming. I stood at the corner of the garage and watched her for I don't know how long. Long enough that I realized I'd been holding my breath. She looked up. She saw me. She said: "I didn't hear you pull in." I said: "I just got here." She said: "I'm getting this damn grass out of my father's bed." I said: "I can see that." She said: "Go in the shed and get me the small pruners. The ones with the green handles." I got the pruners. I knelt down next to her in the dirt. We worked the rose bed for the next hour and a half. We didn't talk about the supplement. We didn't talk about the drawer. We didn't talk about Dr. Patel or the fourteen months or the six years. We just worked the bed. When we were done she stood up — without using her hands to push herself off the ground — and she looked at the bed and she said: "There. That's better." I drove home that night and pulled over at a Kwik Trip about twenty minutes from my house because I was crying too hard to drive. I'm not a crier. I'm an accountant. I cried at my wedding and at my father's funeral and at the birth of each of my kids. That's the list. This was a fifth thing. That was nine months ago. She's been at Dr. Patel's now three times since. Her numbers are in better shape than they've been in a few years. Patel said the combination — the supplement, the fact that she's actually showing up, the small changes she's making in her kitchen — is doing something good. He didn't say it like a miracle had happened. He said it the way a doctor says it when his patient finally decided to show up. I'm not going to give you specific numbers because I don't have permission from my mother to share specific numbers, and also because it doesn't matter. What matters is that she's showing up at her own house. She's showing up at our Sunday dinners. She showed up at Ethan's varsity game in October — drove herself, sat through both halves, ate a hot dog. She made the pies for Thanksgiving. She made them at her own house. She drove them over. She told Hannah she'd teach her the roll recipe in the spring. I want to be careful about what I'm claiming, and I want to be honest about a thing I should have said earlier. I'm not a doctor. I'm not in healthcare. I'm one 47-year-old accountant in Wisconsin who watched her mother shrink for five years after her father died, and finally figured out — late, embarrassingly late — that part of what was happening was that her mother had stopped going to her own doctor's appointments. The supplement is part of what changed. So is showing up at the appointments. So is having a daughter who finally said something. So is my mother deciding, on some Tuesday in May at her own kitchen table, that she wasn't going to hide from her own bloodwork anymore. I can't tell you which of those things did the most work. What I can tell you is that the combination put my mother back in her father's rose bed. If something I've said sounds familiar — if you've got a mother who's been "managing" something for a few years, who's been getting smaller in ways nobody can quite name, who has a drawer somewhere in her kitchen full of envelopes you're not supposed to know about — the only thing I'd encourage you to do is have a conversation. Not about the medication. Not about the supplement. About the appointments. When was the last one. When's the next one. Has she been going. If she's been going, you have nothing to worry about and you can stop reading this and go do something else. If she hasn't been going, you have a different conversation to have. I had mine in a kitchen in May. It didn't go well in the moment. It went well eventually. ~ Karen R. P.S. — Rosabella has a 90-day money-back guarantee. She told me she didn't feel anything for the first three weeks. She told me she felt "a little different" around week five. She told me she felt "more like myself" sometime in the second month. She wouldn't have told me any of that without me asking, by the way. She would have kept it to herself. Mothers like mine don't volunteer information about themselves. You have to ask. Prof. dr Vujković je priznati neurolog sa dugogodišnjim iskustvom u dijagnostici i lečenju bolesti nervnog sistema, a pregled u ovom centru osigurava vrhunski kvalitet i pažljiv pristup svakom pacijentu. **Kako izgleda pregled neurologa?** Pregled neurologa započinje detaljnom anamnezom, gde neurolog postavlja pitanja u vezi sa vašim simptomima, istorijom bolesti, porodičnom istorijom i eventualnim predispozicijama za neurološke poremećaje. Ovaj razgovor je ključan za postavljanje tačne dijagnoze i dalji tok lečenja. Nakon toga, neurolog vrši temeljni neurološki pregled, koji uključuje procenu refleksa, snage mišića, koordinacije, ravnoteže, vida i drugih neuroloških funkcija. Ovaj deo pregleda omogućava lekaru da uoči eventualne poremećaje u funkcionisanju nervnog sistema, kao što su problemi sa moždanim funkcijama, perifernim nervima, mišićima i drugim delovima tela. Nakon osnovnog neurološkog pregleda, ukoliko je potrebno, neurolog može preporučiti dodatne dijagnostičke testove kao što su EEG (elektroencefalogram), EMG (elektromiografija), ili Doppler ultrazvuk krvnih sudova. **Doppler krvnih sudova glave i vrata:** Jedan od ključnih preventivnih pregleda koji se obavljaju u Specijalističkom centru Dr Vulić je Doppler ultrazvuk krvnih sudova glave i vrata. Ovaj test je neinvazivan i koristi zvučne talase za procenu protoka krvi kroz arterije koje snabdevaju mozak. Doppler ultrazvuk je izuzetno važan za rano otkrivanje problema poput suženja ili blokada krvnih sudova (ateroskleroza, tromboza, plikovi), koji mogu dovesti do ozbiljnih neuroloških poremećaja kao što su moždani udar ili TIA (privremeni ishemijski napad). **Zašto je važno raditi Doppler ultrazvuk preventivno?** Doppler ultrazvuk krvnih sudova glave i vrata omogućava pravovremeno otkrivanje potencijalnih problema u krvotoku koji mogu uzrokovati ozbiljne posledice. Mnogi pacijenti nemaju nikakve simptome sve dok ne dođe do ozbiljnog poremećaja. Preporučuje se svim osobama, naročito onima starijim od 50 godina, sa visokim krvnim pritiskom, dijabetesom, povišenim holesterolom, pušačima, kao i onima sa porodičnom istorijom moždanih udara i srčanih oboljenja, da redovno rade ovaj preventivni pregled. **Zakažite pregled bez čekanja!** Ne čekajte da simptomi postanu ozbiljni. Zakažite pregled u Specijalističkom centru Dr Vulić i osigurajte zdravlje svog nervnog sistema. Pozovite nas odmah na broj 051 266 690 i rezervišite termin bez čekanja. Cuoci i 4 topinambur a vapore finché sono morbidi. Pela e frulla con un filo d’olio e sale, ottenendo una crema liscia. 2. In un tegame fai un soffritto con olio e scalogno tritato. In un pentolino scalda un cucchiaio di olio con rosmarino e aglio per ottenere un olio aromatizzato. 7.     Impiatta la fregola cremosa, aggiungi le chips croccanti e qualche goccia di olio profumato. #chefellen #guthealth #gutdriven #seedcrackers #healthieralternatives ✨Savory Seed Crackers 🌱⅓ cup chia seeds 🌱⅓ cup whole flax seeds 🌱⅓ cup sunflower seeds 🌱⅔ cup pumpkin seeds 🌱¼ cup ground flaxseed 🌱2 heaping tablespoons brown rice flour 🌱½ teaspoon baking powder 🌱¼ teaspoon xanthan or guar gum 🌱Garlic powder, to taste 🌱Onion powder, to taste 🌱Sea salt, to taste 🌱2 tablespoons refined coconut oil, melted 🌱⅓ cup warm water, plus more as needed 🌱Optional: dried oregano, finely chopped fresh rosemary, or dried basil Preheat oven to 325°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. For a cracker that holds together particularly well, lightly pulse the pumpkin and sunflower seeds in a food processor just a few times. You want them roughly broken up, not ground into flour. In a large bowl, combine the chia, flax, sunflower, and pumpkin seeds, ground flaxseed, brown rice flour, baking powder, xanthan or guar gum, and seasonings. Stir in the melted coconut oil and ⅓ cup warm water. Mix thoroughly. Allow the mixture to rest for 15 minutes so the chia and flax can absorb the water and create a natural gel. Check the consistency. The mixture should be thick, slightly sticky, and hold together when pressed. If it seems dry or crumbly, add additional warm water 1 tablespoon at a time. Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking sheet. Place another sheet of parchment on top and roll or press evenly to approximately ⅛-inch thick. Remove the top parchment and score into desired cracker shapes. Bake for approximately 25–30 minutes, or until the cracker sheet feels set and the edges are beginning to crisp. Carefully separate or flip the crackers and return them to the oven for another 10–15 minutes, until dry and crisp. They will become even crisper as they cool. Note: Don’t rush the 15-minute rest. I worked as a paralegal at the same small law firm in our town from 1981 until I retired at sixty-three. I have been retired for seven years and I have used those seven years carefully. I tell you all of this because the story I want to tell you is not a dramatic story. It is the story of a woman who has been paying patient, quiet attention to her cardiovascular wellness for twenty-three years, and who added one small thing to her mornings a little over a year ago that she wanted to mention to other women like her. I want to start with what I have been doing for the last twenty-three years, because the rest of this letter does not make sense without it. When I was forty-seven, my mother died. She was sixty-eight. She had a heart event in October and a second one in December and she was gone by February. My mother had spent most of her life, by her own admission, not paying very much attention to her cardiovascular wellness. She had eaten the way women of her generation ate, smoked from her twenties to her fifties, walked when she needed to and not when she didn't, and the cardiovascular medications she had been put on in her early sixties had been a too-late addition to a body that had been telling her things she had not been listening to. I sat with all of that for a long time after she died. When I was forty-seven and a half, I went to my own doctor and asked her, plainly, what a woman in her late forties could start doing to make sure she did not have my mother's last few months at sixty-eight.

👴Volám sa Ján Novák. Mám 68 rokov a žijem v Bratislave na Slovensku 🇸🇰. Som starý otec Sofie. Ja mám bielu pokožku, a moja vnučka Sofia má tmavšiu pokožku. Ale pre mňa to nikdy nebolo to prvé, čo som na nej videl. Pre mňa bola vždy jednoducho moja malá Sofia. Dievčatko, ktoré ku mne vždy bežalo do náručia v záhrade. Dievčatko, ktoré sa ma vždy pýtalo: „Dedko, ešte jednu rozprávku pred spaním.“ Dievčatko, ktoré ma objímalo okolo krku a hovorilo: „Dedko, ešte jedno objatie.“ ❤️ A ako mnoho starých rodičov, aj ja som mal pre ňu obrovskú slabosť. Príliš som ju rozmaznával. Pizza 🍕 Hranolky 🍟 Sladké nápoje 🥤 Sušienky po škole. Malé maškrty cez víkendy. Zakaždým, keď sa usmiala, mal som pocit, že robím niečo dobré. Tak som si opakoval: „Je to len dieťa.“ „Zaslúži si užívať si.“ „Časom sa to zmení.“ Ale postupne som si začal všímať malé zmeny. Sofia mala menej energie. Bola pokojnejšia. Už nebehala tak ako predtým. Radšej si viac oddýchla. A niektoré aktivity, ktoré mala kedysi rada, jej začali robiť trochu väčší problém. Najskôr som sa snažil nerobiť si starosti. Až jedného popoludnia… sa všetko zmenilo. Išli sme po schodoch v mojom dome. V polovici cesty sa zastavila. Chytila sa zábradlia, pozrela dole a ticho mi povedala: „Dedko… som unavená.“ Tá veta vo mne zostala. Nie preto, že by nemohla pokračovať… ale preto, že som si zrazu uvedomil jednu vec: Pomýlil som si lásku s tým, že jej stále dávam malé odmeny. Dal som jej veľa šťastných chvíľ, ale možno nie dosť zdravých návykov. Dal som jej veľa lásky, ale nie dosť rovnováhy. A jej malé telo mi to začínalo ukazovať. Nikdy nešlo iba o vzhľad. Išlo o: ✨ Energiu ✨ Sebavedomie ✨ Každodenné návyky ✨ Pohodu A o to, ako sa začínala cítiť sama so sebou. Vedeli sme, že musíme niektoré veci zmeniť. Ale mal som jednu veľmi jasnú vec: Nechcel som, aby Sofia cítila hanbu. Nechcel som prísne diéty. Nechcel som, aby pohyb vyzeral ako trest. A nikdy som nechcel, aby sa pozerala do zrkadla so smútkom. Chcel som len, aby sa opäť cítila: silnejšia, aktívnejšia, a šťastná taká, aká je. ❤️ Potom sme sa rozhodli začať malými zmenami. S podporou odborníkov na zdravie detí sme sa naučili niečo veľmi dôležité: 👉„U detí nie sú najdôležitejšie extrémne metódy. Najdôležitejšie sú malé každodenné návyky: vyvážená strava, viac pohybu, dostatok kvalitného spánku a veľa emocionálnej podpory.“ Táto veta zmenila môj pohľad na všetko. Keď sme sa vrátili domov, dal som si sľub: Tentoraz ju nebudem iba rozmaznávať. Budem ju sprevádzať. Bez tlaku. Bez hádok. Bez výčitiek. Len s trpezlivosťou, láskou a vytrvalosťou. Tak sme začali postupne: 💧 Viac vody. 🥗 Vyváženejšie jedlá. 🍎 Menej automatického maškrtenia. 🏡 Viac domácich jedál. 🚶 Krátke prechádzky po večeri. 🌙 Pravidelnejší čas spánku. A jedno jediné pravidlo: „Dnes musíme urobiť iba jedno dobré rozhodnutie.“ Na začiatku sa nič nezdalo výnimočné. Ale po niekoľkých týždňoch sme začali vidieť malé zmeny: ✔ Pýtala si menej sladkostí ✔ Mala viac energie ✔ Pohybovala sa ľahšie ✔ Cítila sa pohodlnejšie vo svojom oblečení ✔ Častejšie sa usmievala Po určitom čase sme nevideli iba fyzické zmeny. Najkrajšie bolo vidieť, ako sa jej vracia sebavedomie. Jedného popoludnia Sofia pribehla ku mne v záhrade s obrovským úsmevom a veľmi silno ma objala. 🤗 A tentoraz… som ju dokázal opäť zdvihnúť bez toho, aby som cítil, že je to pre mňa náročné. Ten moment ma naučil niečo dôležité: Nikdy nešlo iba o číslo na váhe. Išlo o to dať mojej vnučke príležitosť vyrastať s pocitom, že je silná, sebavedomá, šťastná a hlboko milovaná. Nysgjerrig på kokeboka mi «Opptur med sunne middagar»? La meg dele innholdet i kortversjon🥰 Det spørsmålet eg oftast får, er kva oppskrifter boka inneholder - og det ligger litt i tittelen: dette er ei middagsbok! Middagsbok med fokus på sunne, raske og enkle kvardagsmiddager + litt ekstra 🙂 Det eg personlig liker aller best er kapittelinndelinga, der lesaren kan finne ein fristande oppskrift i det kapittelet som passer best: → Middagar på maks 20 minutt → Middagar ein kan lage klar kvelden før → Alt-i-eitt midddagar → Restemiddagar → Middagar for ein person → Middagar med maks 6 ingredienser → Helgemiddagar → Tilbehørtips til middagen Genialt, eller kva? Det synes vertfall eg! Eg vil og få fram at boka har stor variasjon i oppskriftene: alt fra kjøtt, fisk, kylling og vegetar i ulike oppskrifter som suppe, gryte, grateng, salater, tallerkenretter m.m🥙 Boka inneholder 80 oppskrifter, der over halvparten (ca 45 av dei) ikkje er delt på bloggen tidligare. Av desse oppskriftene har eg satt sammen 10 forskjellige vekemenyer MED tilhøyrande handleliste også🤩👏🏻 I tillegg vil eg få fram at ein trenger ikkje noken spesialingredienser, kun vanlige ingredienser fra dagligvarebutikken - og ikkje minst at alle oppskriftene er merka med symbol som viser om oppskrifta er glutenfri/melkefri/vegetarisk💛 Må og nevne at det her er meir enn berre ei kokebok, med mange ulike tekster med tips & råd til korleis ein skal ta bedre valg når det kjem til matvalg, planlegging, sparing av penger, unngå matsvinn og bruke opp matrestene👏🏻 Så, kort fortalt er dette boka for oss som sliter med tidsklemma, som syns middagsmat er ei utfordring, og for oss som treng inspirasjon til å løfte middagen til nye høgder på ein enkel måte! Bli med på en uforglemmelig reise for kropp, sinn og sjel. Midt i den mørke og kalde vinteren i Norge inviteres du med på en yoga ferie-retreat i Goa – som kombinerer yoga, sol, varme, strand & hav , rom for hvile og velvære , og Indisk kultur fellesskap. Dette er en reise for å varme kroppen, roe sinnet og fylle på med lys, varme og NY ENERGI, i idylliske omgivelser ved havet i Mandrem, Nord-Goa. Om retreatet Retreatet holdes på Nalanda Retreat i Nord-Goa, et veletablert og anerkjent yogasenter rett ved stranden. Her skaper vi en trygg, rolig og inkluderende ramme rundt dagene – hvor yoga, strand & hav -og indisk tradisjon smelter sammen. Retreatet starter lørdag 20. februar (morgen) og avsluttes lørdag 27. februar (kveld).  Avreise fra Norge fredag 19. februar, og retur søndag 28 februar-27 Ønsker du et lengre opphold i Goa, kan du gjerne komme noen dager før eller bli litt lenger etter retreatet. Arrangøren kan være behjelpelig med overnatting og praktisk planlegging, enten i Goa eller andre destinasjoner i India. Om du ønsker kan du selvsagt kombinere yogaretreatet med litt reising i India, enten før eller etter oppholdet i Goa ! ⸻ Yoga & daglig rytme Yogaen vil være variert og tilgjengelig – fra litt mer aktiv morgenyoga til rolig, nærende og restorativ praksis. Det vil være flere yogatimer daglig gjennom 8 dager , tilpasset gruppen og energien i retreatet. Dagene har en naturlig og behagelig rytme: – Yoga og morgenpraksis – Deilig frokost ved stranden, i retreatets åpne lounge – Tid til strandliv, hvile og egentid – Enkelte dager felles utflukter – Rolig samling eller myk yoga på ettermiddag – Felles middag ved stranden På kvelden er det også mulighet for meditasjon, chanting og beachfire ved stranden. Retreatet åpnes og avsluttes med en tradisjonell pooja-seremoni, ledet av en lokal hindu. Seremonien brukes til å samle gruppen, skape felles fokus og markere starten og avslutningen på oppholdet på en jordnær og meningsfull måte. Du trenger absolutt ingen tidligere erfaring med yoga. Dette retreatet passer for alle. ⸻ Måltider Måltidene er en viktig del av retreatopplevelsen og støtter rytmen gjennom dagen. Maten på Nalanda Retreat er vegetarisk, med innslag av fisk, og tilberedt med fokus på ferske, lokale og sesongbaserte råvarer. Frokost og middag nytes i retreatets åpne restaurant ved stranden og gir rom for både ro, samtale og fellesskap. ⸻ Opplevelser & fellesskap I tillegg til yoga og egentid inngår felles opplevelser og utflukter i retreatprogrammet. Eksempler på opplevelser kan være: – Sunrise dolphin boat trip – Friday Night Market – Besøk i Old Goa – Felles tempelbesøk *Disse opplevelsene betales separat. ⸻ Spa & velvære Nalanda Retreat har eget spa med ayurvedisk helsekonsultasjon, massasje og holistiske behandlinger. ad_text: En musikalisk helkväll i samarbete med Hållandsgården. I orostider när många känner rädsla och hjälplöshet kan det egna skapandet, mötet med naturen och gemenskap med andra människor ge oss perspektiv, kraft och inspiration att se framåt. Det är mot den fonden som föreställningen Förnimmelser har vuxit fram och tagit form. Genom poesi, musik och sång vill vi lyfta både egna och några av samtidens mångfacetterade frågor och känslor för att på så sätt få syn på dem. I föreställningen flätas orden samman med musiken till en helhet som bär på en önskan att lyfta hoppet och stärka motståndskraften så att vi tillsammans kan föreställa oss och forma en ljusare framtid. Marianne Folkedotter är berättare, poet och låtskrivare som i en rad uppmärksammade och uppskattade berättarföreställningar visat sin förmåga att med orden upplysa, entusiasmera och förundra en stor publik i och utanför Västerbotten. 2022 debuterade hon med diktsamlingen ”En skog som går omkring bland husen” som sedan iscensattes med musik av och med Rickard N Jokela. Rickard N Jokela är basist och kompositör med influenser från jazz, indisk raga och modern konstmusik. Efter resor i bland annat Japan, Indien och Schweiz har han utvecklat ett eget förhållande till improvisation och komposition med just solospel i fokus. Konserten arrangeras i samarbete med Hållandsgården som erbjuder vegetarisk buffé innan föreställningen. I del ett låter vi några av alla de människor vi mött under året ta plats och berätta om sina liv, modiga och starka berättelser om livsvägar som varit allt annat än raka men som lett till förändring. I del två lämnar vi plats åt medarbetarna i våra verksamheter, som varje dag jobbar för att stötta människorna vi möter till självständighet och egenmakt. Här finns också vår årsredovisning. I del tre gör vi nedslag i alla våra verksamheter under ett dygn, från tidig morgon på Ringövarvet till sen natt med Skyddsbussen, verksamheter som alla arbetar utifrån våra tre grundpelare; rätt till en trygg bostad, möjlighet till meningsfull sysselsättning och hjälp till en god psykisk hälsa. Att vi vinner priser för vår kommunikation är förstås otroligt roligt, hedrande och uppmuntrande. Men viktigast av allt är att verksamhetsberättelsen lyckas nå ut med vår värdegrund: respekten för alla människors lika värde och tron på varje människas vilja och förmåga att styra sitt eget liv. Och att fler får läsa om idéburen sektor och organisationer som Skyddsvärnet, som behövs minst lika mycket idag som när vi grundades för 110 år sedan. Ladda ner den här: https://skyddsvarnet.org/organisationen/ eller hör av dig om du vill ha ett tryckt ex!
